Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that being a new mom can be a truly overwhelming and life-changing experience. It's completely normal to have a wide range of emotions during this time, and I'm here to support you in any way I can.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns that may be affecting your well-being during the postpartum period. The purpose of this assessment is to provide a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings, and to help us work together to ensure you're getting the care and support you need.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and respected. I'm here to listen and support you without judgment, and I want you to feel comfortable sharing your thoughts and feelings with me. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better understanding of your emotional experience over the past 7 days.

We'll take this one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible. So, let's get started. The first question is: Over the past 7 days, how have you been feeling about yourself, and have you been able to enjoy the things you usually enjoy?

.. to be honest, I've been feeling a bit overwhelmed and tired most of the time. Taking care of the baby is a lot of work, and I'm not getting as much sleep as I'd like. Some days, I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm doing everything I need to do, but I don't really feel like I'm enjoying it as much as I thought I would. Like, I used to love reading and taking walks, but lately, I just haven't had the energy or the time for those things. And when I do try to do something I enjoy, I feel guilty because I think I should be spending that time with the baby instead.

I do have moments where I feel happy and connected to my baby, though. Like, when she smiles at me or falls asleep in my arms, it's just the best feeling in the world. But those moments are kind of fleeting, and then I'm back to feeling anxious and worried about whether I'm doing everything right. I worry about her health, and whether I'm feeding her enough, or if I'm doing enough to stimulate her development... it's just a lot of pressure, you know? And sometimes, I feel like I'm not doing a good enough job, and that's hard for me to deal with. But, like I said, it's not all bad. I'm just... tired, and a little unsure of myself, I guess.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I'd say that's only happened a few times over the past week. I mean, I've smiled and laughed with my partner or family members, but it's not like it used to be. I feel like I've lost a bit of my sense of humor, to be honest. Most of the time, I'm just trying to get through the day and make sure the baby is okay. I don't really have the energy to laugh or find the funny side of things like I used to.

But, there was one time when my baby did something really cute, like she made this silly face at me, and I couldn't help but laugh. It was just a little moment, but it was nice to feel that way again, even if it was just for a second. It's like, I know I should be enjoying this time and finding the humor in things, but it's just not coming as easily as it used to. Does that make sense.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I'll think about something I want to do, like take a shower or have a cup of coffee, and I'll look forward to it for a little while. But then the baby will need something, or I'll start worrying about her, and it's like my mind gets pulled away from thinking about those things. And sometimes, even when I do get to do something I've been looking forward to, it's just not as enjoyable as it used to be.

Like, my partner and I were going to watch a movie together last night, and I was really looking forward to it. But then the baby woke up and needed to be fed, and by the time we got her back to sleep, I was just too tired to care about the movie anymore. So, we ended up just going to bed instead. It's like, I know I should be looking forward to things and enjoying them, but it's just hard to do that when I'm so tired and preoccupied with the baby's needs all the time.

I do try to plan little things for myself, like taking a walk or reading a book, but it's hard to get excited about them when I know that the baby might need me at any moment. It's like, I'm always on call, you know? And that makes it hard to really look forward to things or enjoy them when they happen.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... I'd say that's happened a few times over the past week. I mean, if the baby cries and I don't know why, or if she's not feeding well, I immediately start thinking that it's my fault. Like, I'm not doing something right, or I'm not good enough. It's like, I put a lot of pressure on myself to be perfect, and when things don't go according to plan, I get really hard on myself.

Like, the other day, I was trying to get the baby to latch, and she just wasn't having it. And I got so frustrated with myself, thinking that I was doing something wrong, that I wasn't good enough to even feed my own baby. It was a really tough moment, and I felt like I was failing her. But, looking back, I realize that it's just one of those things that happens sometimes, and it's not necessarily my fault.

It's hard for me to shake off that feeling of self-blame, though. I feel like I'm constantly second-guessing myself, wondering if I'm doing everything right. And if something goes wrong, I immediately start thinking that it's because of something I did or didn't do. It's exhausting, to be honest. And it makes me feel really anxious and uncertain about my ability to take care of my baby.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's been happening a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something. Like, what if she gets sick? What if I'm not producing enough milk? What if I'm not doing enough to stimulate her development? It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I get really anxious.

And the thing is, it's not even like there's a real reason for me to be worried. The baby is healthy, she's growing well, and she's happy. But my mind just can't seem to shut off, you know? I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and I'll get this knot in my stomach. It's really hard to calm myself down and reassure myself that everything is okay.

Sometimes, I'll be out with the baby, and I'll see another mom with her baby, and I'll start comparing myself to her. Like, is she a better mom than me? Is her baby healthier than mine? It's just this constant feeling of uncertainty and self-doubt, and it's really hard to shake off.

I've also been having these random, scary thoughts, like what if something happens to the baby while I'm sleeping? What if I forget to do something important? It's like, my brain is just constantly on the lookout for potential dangers, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's hard to enjoy the moment, you know, when I'm always worried about what might happen next.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. It's like, my body is responding to some kind of threat, but there's no real reason for it.

It's really scary, because I don't know what's happening or why I'm feeling that way. And it's hard to calm myself down, because my mind is racing and I'm thinking about all the worst-case scenarios. Like, what if something's wrong with the baby? What if I'm not a good enough mom?

Sometimes, it happens when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll start feeling overwhelmed and anxious. I'll think, "What if I'm not doing this right? What if I'm messing everything up?" And then I'll start to feel panicky, like I'm in way over my head.

It's not all the time, but it's happened enough that it's started to worry me. I'll be going about my day, feeling fine, and then suddenly I'll feel this panic rising up. It's like, my body is trying to tell me something, but I don't know what.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but it's hard to explain. I feel like I'm just being paranoid or overreacting, but at the same time, it feels so real and so scary. I just wish I could figure out what's causing it and make it stop. It's like, I'm already feeling so overwhelmed and anxious about being a new mom, and then these panic feelings just make it worse.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's definitely been true for me lately. I feel like I'm just trying to keep my head above water, you know? Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I'm not getting enough sleep, and even when I do get a chance to rest, my mind is always racing with worries about the baby or the household or something else.

Sometimes, it feels like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. I'll be trying to do one thing, like laundry or dishes, and then the baby will need something, and I'll have to drop everything to take care of her. And then I'll feel guilty for not getting the other things done, and it just feels like I'm failing all around.

I've been trying to prioritize and make lists and all that, but it's hard to keep up. And some days, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together. Like, I'll be sitting on the couch, feeding the baby, and I'll just start to feel overwhelmed by everything. The mess, the laundry, the dishes, the baby's needs... it all just feels like too much.

My partner tries to help, but even with their support, it still feels like a lot to handle. And some days, I just feel like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not good enough. It's like, I'm just trying to survive, you know? But at the same time, I want to be a good mom, and I want to take care of my baby, and I want to keep our home running smoothly... it's just a lot of pressure.

I guess what I'm saying is, yeah, things have definitely been getting on top of me lately. It's hard to keep up, and it's hard to feel like I'm doing everything right. But I'm trying, you know? I'm just trying to take it one day at a time, and hope that things get a little easier as time goes on.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been true for me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up. I mean, that's definitely part of it, but even when she's sleeping, I've been having trouble falling asleep or staying asleep. And I think it's because my mind is just racing with worries and thoughts and feelings.

I'll be lying in bed, trying to relax, and suddenly I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do tomorrow, or all the things that could go wrong with the baby. Or I'll start feeling anxious about something, like whether I'm doing a good job as a mom, or whether I'm meeting all of the baby's needs. And then I'll start to feel overwhelmed, and my mind will just start spinning with all these negative thoughts.

It's hard to calm myself down and relax when I'm feeling like that. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll often wake up in the middle of the night, feeling anxious or worried about something. It's like, my mind is just constantly on the go, even when my body is trying to rest.

I've tried to establish a bedtime routine, and I've tried to create a relaxing sleep environment, but it's just not working. I've even tried taking warm baths, or practicing deep breathing exercises, but nothing seems to be helping. I just feel like I'm stuck in this cycle of anxiety and worry, and it's affecting my sleep.

It's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, though. It's the fact that I'm feeling so unhappy and overwhelmed all the time. I mean, I know that being a new mom is supposed to be a happy and exciting time, but for me, it's just been really tough. I feel like I'm just struggling to keep my head above water, and it's taking a toll on my mental health.

I guess what I'm saying is, yes, I have been so unhappy that I've had difficulty sleeping. And it's not just the sleep deprivation that's the problem, it's the underlying feelings of anxiety and overwhelm that are causing it.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... I'd say that's been true for me more often than not lately. I mean, I'll have moments where I'm feeling okay, and I'll be playing with the baby or doing something I enjoy, and then suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's like, I'll be crying for no reason, or I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of misery.

It's hard to explain, because it's not like anything's necessarily wrong. The baby's healthy, my partner's supportive, we have a good home... it's just, I don't know, I feel like I've lost myself or something. Like, I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really feeling like myself.

Sometimes, I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just start crying because I feel so overwhelmed. Or I'll be doing something simple, like making a bottle or changing a diaper, and I'll just start feeling this deep sadness. It's like, I'm grieving the loss of my old life or something.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, and they've been really supportive, but it's hard to explain. They'll say things like, "You're a great mom," or "You're doing a wonderful job," but it's hard to feel that way when I'm feeling so sad and miserable all the time.

I guess what I'm saying is, yes, I have felt sad or miserable. It's not all the time, but it's often enough that it's starting to feel like a pattern. And it's hard to shake, because it feels like it's just a part of who I am now. Like, I'm just a sad, miserable person, and that's not who I used to be. I used to be happy, and carefree, and now I just feel like I'm struggling to get through each day.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... that's been true for me lately. I've been crying a lot, and it's not just because I'm tired or overwhelmed, although that's definitely part of it. It's just that I feel so much emotion all the time, and it's hard to keep it all inside.

I'll be doing something simple, like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's like, the emotions just build up and then they overflow, and I'll be sobbing uncontrollably. It's really embarrassing, actually, because sometimes my partner will be like, "What's wrong?" and I'll be like, "I don't know, I just am."

It's not just the big things that make me cry, either. It's the little things, like when the baby won't latch or when I'm feeling really overwhelmed. It's like, my emotions are just really close to the surface all the time, and it doesn't take much to set me off.

I've been trying to be kind to myself, and to remind myself that it's okay to feel this way. But it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this happy, capable mom, and instead I'm just a mess. I feel like I'm failing, or that there's something wrong with me, because I'm not feeling the way I'm supposed to feel.

I guess what I'm saying is, yes, I have been so unhappy that I've been crying. A lot. It's not something I'm proud of, but it's just the way I'm feeling right now. And I'm hoping that by talking about it, I can start to work through some of these emotions and feel better.

* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
